title: English Grammar Assessment Grade 6 (Grammar Gr.6 - MidFinal)

sections.name: Section A: Multiple Choice (ปรนัย)
Section B: True / False (ถูก / ผิด)
Section C: Scenario-Based (สถานการณ์จำลอง)
Section D: Short Answer (อัตนัย / อธิบายความรู้)

questions.question: The Earth ________ around the Sun.
questions.explanation: General scientific facts take Present Simple Tense with singular subject Earth -> revolves.

questions.question: Listen! Someone ________ on the front door.
questions.explanation: The signal word 'Listen!' indicates an action happening now -> Present Continuous (is knocking).

questions.question: She ________ her keys in the car yesterday afternoon.
questions.explanation: Past Simple signal word 'yesterday' requires V.2 of leave -> left.

questions.question: Look at those dark clouds! It ________ rain soon.
questions.explanation: Predictions based on present evidence (dark clouds) use 'be going to' -> is going to.

questions.question: I ________ lived in Bangkok for five years.
questions.explanation: Present Perfect tense with Subject 'I' uses have + V.3 -> have lived.

questions.question: Either Tom or his brothers ________ responsible for locking the gate.
questions.explanation: With 'either...or', the verb agrees with the closest subject 'his brothers' (plural) -> are.

questions.question: Neither of the two books ________ interesting.
questions.explanation: 'Neither of + plural noun' takes a singular verb -> is.

questions.question: Bread and butter ________ my favorite breakfast.
questions.explanation: Bread and butter considered as a single compound meal takes a singular verb -> is.

questions.question: Every boy and girl in the class ________ a textbook.
questions.explanation: Subject modified by 'Every' takes a singular verb -> has.

questions.question: A number of students ________ absent today, but the number of absent students ________ decreasing.
questions.explanation: 'A number of' takes plural verb (are); 'The number of' takes singular verb (is).

questions.question: Choose the correct plural form of the word 'hypothesis'.
questions.explanation: Nouns ending in -is change to -es in plural -> hypotheses.

questions.question: Which of the following is an UNCOUNTABLE noun?
questions.explanation: Furniture is an uncountable category noun.

questions.question: The little boy fell down and hurt ________.
questions.explanation: When subject and object are the same person, use reflexive pronoun -> himself.

questions.question: The girl ________ wallet was stolen called the police.
questions.explanation: Possessive relative pronoun referring to the girl's wallet -> whose.

questions.question: This is the university ________ my father studied engineering.
questions.explanation: Relative pronoun referring to a place where an action occurred -> where.

questions.question: He speaks English very ________ because he practiced hard.
questions.explanation: An adverb (fluently) modifies the verb speaks.

questions.question: This puzzle is much ________ than the previous one.
questions.explanation: Two-syllable adjective ending in -y changes to -ier in comparative -> easier.

questions.question: She is ________ student in our entire school.
questions.explanation: Superlative degree requires 'the most intelligent'.

questions.question: Where should the adverb 'always' be placed in this sentence: 'She (1) is (2) punctual (3) for work (4)'?
questions.explanation: Adverbs of frequency go AFTER verb 'to be' (is always punctual).

questions.question: Which phrase shows correct possessive punctuation for plural boys?
questions.explanation: Plural regular nouns ending in -s take apostrophe after s -> boys'.

questions.question: We have been studying English ________ 2021.
questions.explanation: 'since' is used with a specific starting point in time (2021).

questions.question: They lived in London ________ three years.
questions.explanation: 'for' is used with a duration/period of time (three years).

questions.question: The cat is sleeping ________ the rug in front of the fireplace.
questions.explanation: Surfaces take preposition 'on' -> on the rug.

questions.question: He is ________ honest man who always tells ________ truth.
questions.explanation: 'honest' has silent 'h' (starts with vowel sound -> an); 'the truth' is a fixed idiom.

questions.question: ________ Lead is a heavy metal.
questions.explanation: Uncountable nouns used in a general sense take no article.

questions.question: There are ________ books on the shelf, but not many.
questions.explanation: Countable plural nouns (books) in small quantity take 'a few'.

questions.question: Could you please add ________ sugar to my coffee?
questions.explanation: Uncountable nouns (sugar) in small quantity take 'a little'.

questions.question: ________ it was raining heavily, we went out for a walk.
questions.explanation: Subordinating conjunction showing concession/contrast -> Although.

questions.question: Study hard, ________ you will fail the final examination.
questions.explanation: Conjunction 'or' expresses negative alternative outcome.

questions.question: Not only did he pass the exam, ________ he also won first prize.
questions.explanation: Correlative conjunction pair: 'Not only... but also'.

questions.question: You haven't finished your homework yet, ________?
questions.explanation: Negative main clause (haven't) takes positive tag -> have you?

questions.question: Let's go for a walk in the park, ________?
questions.explanation: Suggestions with 'Let's' take question tag 'shall we?'.

questions.question: Nobody called while I was out, ________?
questions.explanation: 'Nobody' makes clause negative and takes pronoun 'they' -> positive tag 'did they?'.

questions.question: You ________ smoke in the hospital. It is strictly prohibited.
questions.explanation: Strict legal prohibition uses 'mustn't'.

questions.question: Tomorrow is Sunday. I ________ get up early.
questions.explanation: Absence of necessity/obligation uses 'don't have to'.

questions.question: He has been working all day without rest. He ________ be exhausted.
questions.explanation: Strong positive logical deduction uses 'must'.

questions.question: English ________ in many countries around the world.
questions.explanation: Present Simple passive: is + V.3 (is spoken).

questions.question: The telephone ________ by Alexander Graham Bell in 1876.
questions.explanation: Past Simple passive singular object: was + V.3 (was invented).

questions.question: Active: 'The chef prepares dinner.' -> Passive: 'Dinner ________ by the chef.'
questions.explanation: Present Simple active 'prepares' converts to passive 'is prepared'.

questions.question: Active: 'Somebody stole my bicycle.' -> Passive: 'My bicycle ________.'
questions.explanation: Past Simple active 'stole' converts to passive 'was stolen'.

questions.question: If you heat ice, it ________.
questions.explanation: Zero conditional for general scientific facts: If + Present Simple, Present Simple -> melts.

questions.question: If she ________ hard, she will pass the exam.
questions.explanation: First conditional: If + Present Simple (studies), Will + V.1.

questions.question: Unless you ________ now, you will miss the train.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' means 'If... not', so it takes a positive verb form -> leave.

questions.question: Which sentence uses commas correctly in a list?

options.ก: I bought apples oranges and bananas.
options.ข: I bought apples, oranges, and bananas.
options.ค: I bought, apples, oranges, and bananas.
options.ง: I bought apples oranges, and bananas.

questions.explanation: Items in a list are separated by commas (Oxford comma before 'and').

questions.question: Choose the sentence with correct apostrophe usage for contractions.

options.ก: Its raining outside, so dont forget your umbrella.
options.ข: It's raining outside, so don't forget your umbrella.
options.ค: Its' raining outside, so dont' forget your umbrella.
options.ง: It'is raining outside, so do'nt forget your umbrella.

questions.explanation: It's = It is; don't = do not.

questions.question: The cat licked ________ paws after eating ________ food.
questions.explanation: Possessive adjective is 'its' (without apostrophe).

questions.question: ________ going to visit ________ grandparents over ________.
questions.explanation: They're = They are; their = possessive; there = location.

questions.question: If ________ ready, we can start ________ exam now.
questions.explanation: you're = you are; your = possessive adjective.

questions.question: Identify the grammatically INCORRECT part: 'She don't (A) like (B) playing (C) tennis (D).'
questions.explanation: Singular subject 'She' requires 'doesn't', not 'don't'.

questions.question: Identify the grammatically INCORRECT part: 'One of my friend (A) is (B) coming (C) today (D).'
questions.explanation: 'One of + plural noun' requires 'friends', not 'friend'.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly avoids a double negative?

options.ก: I don't know nothing about it.
options.ข: I don't know anything about it.

questions.explanation: Standard English avoids double negatives: 'I don't know anything'.

questions.question: Direct: He said, 'I am busy.' -> Indirect: He said that he ________ busy.
questions.explanation: Present Simple 'am' backshifts to Past Simple 'was' in indirect speech.

questions.question: Direct: 'Where do you live?' she asked. -> Indirect: She asked me where I ________.
questions.explanation: Indirect questions use statement word order and backshift tense -> where I lived.

questions.question: She enjoys ________ fantasy novels in her free time.
questions.explanation: The verb 'enjoy' is followed by a gerund (-ing form) -> reading.

questions.question: He decided ________ a new laptop for university.
questions.explanation: The verb 'decide' is followed by an infinitive (to + V.1) -> to buy.

questions.question: When I was a child, I ________ live in a small village.
questions.explanation: Past habits/states no longer true take 'used to + V.1'.

questions.question: Choose the sentence with correct parallel structure.

options.ก: He likes swimming, running, and to bike.
options.ข: He likes swimming, running, and biking.
options.ค: He likes to swim, running, and biking.
options.ง: He likes swim, run, and bike.

questions.explanation: Parallel structure keeps matching grammatical forms (-ing, -ing, -ing).

questions.question: Which word in the sentence requires capitalization: 'we will visit uncle sam in london next tuesday.'?
questions.explanation: Capitalize sentence start (We), proper names (Sam, London), and days (Tuesday).

questions.question: My mother made me ________ my bedroom before going out.
questions.explanation: Causative verb 'make someone + bare infinitive' (clean).

questions.question: I wish I ________ more time to travel the world.
questions.explanation: Present wishes take Past Simple form -> had.

questions.question: The Present Continuous Tense is used for habitual actions and general truths.
questions.explanation: Incorrect. Present Simple is used for habits/truths; Present Continuous is for actions happening now.

questions.question: Plural subjects require plural verbs (e.g., The dogs bark).
questions.explanation: Correct. Subject-verb agreement requires matching numbers.

questions.question: The plural of 'mouse' is 'mouses'.
questions.explanation: Incorrect. The irregular plural of mouse is 'mice'.

questions.question: Information, advice, and news are all uncountable nouns in English.
questions.explanation: Correct. Information, advice, and news take singular verbs and cannot be pluralized with -s.

questions.question: Reflexive pronouns end in '-self' (singular) or '-selves' (plural).
questions.explanation: Correct. E.g., himself, themselves.

questions.question: Adverbs modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs.
questions.explanation: Correct. Definition of adverb functions.

questions.question: The adverb form of 'good' is 'goodly'.
questions.explanation: Incorrect. The adverb form of good is 'well'.

questions.question: We use 'in' for specific times on the clock, e.g., 'in 5 o'clock'.
questions.explanation: Incorrect. Specific clock times take 'at' (at 5 o'clock).

questions.question: We use 'on' for days of the week and specific dates (e.g., on Friday, on May 1st).
questions.explanation: Correct. Days and dates take preposition 'on'.

questions.question: We use 'an' before words that start with a consonant sound.
questions.explanation: Incorrect. We use 'an' before VOWEL sounds (a, e, i, o, u).

questions.question: The definite article 'the' is used when referring to a specific noun known to the listener.
questions.explanation: Correct. 'The' specifies known/unique items.

questions.question: We use 'many' with uncountable nouns in negative sentences.
questions.explanation: Incorrect. We use 'much' with uncountable nouns (much water); 'many' is for countable nouns.

questions.question: The conjunction 'because' shows cause and reason.
questions.explanation: Correct. 'Because' introduces clauses of reason.

questions.question: A positive statement takes a positive question tag.
questions.explanation: Incorrect. A positive statement takes a NEGATIVE tag (She is smart, isn't she?).

questions.question: The modal verb 'can' can express both ability and permission.
questions.explanation: Correct. 'Can' expresses ability (I can swim) and permission (Can I leave?).

questions.question: In passive voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
questions.explanation: Correct. Object -> Subject shift is fundamental to passive voice.

questions.question: First conditional sentences express imaginary or impossible situations in the past.
questions.explanation: Incorrect. First conditional expresses real/possible future situations. Past impossible is Third conditional.

questions.question: An apostrophe is used to show possession and contraction.
questions.explanation: Correct. E.g., Tom's book (possession) and don't (contraction).

questions.question: 'Their' is a contraction for 'they are'.
questions.explanation: Incorrect. 'Their' is possessive. 'They're' is the contraction for 'they are'.

questions.question: A gerund is a verb form ending in -ing that functions as a noun.
questions.explanation: Correct. E.g., Swimming is good exercise.

questions.question: In standard English, using two negative words in the same clause is correct.
questions.explanation: Incorrect. Double negatives (e.g., I don't know nothing) are grammatically incorrect in standard English.

questions.question: The comparative form of 'bad' is 'worse'.
questions.explanation: Correct. Irregular comparative: bad -> worse -> worst.

questions.question: Indefinite pronouns like 'someone', 'everybody', and 'nobody' take plural verbs.
questions.explanation: Incorrect. Indefinite pronouns ending in -one, -body, -thing take SINGULAR verbs.

questions.question: 'Whose' is used to replace possessive adjectives for both people and things.
questions.explanation: Correct. 'Whose' indicates possession in relative clauses.

questions.question: The Past Continuous Tense is formed with 'was/were + V.-ing'.
questions.explanation: Correct. Past Continuous = was/were + V.-ing.

questions.question: We say 'in night' when referring to late evening hours.
questions.explanation: Incorrect. Time phrase is 'at night'.

questions.question: 'Although' and 'despite' have similar meanings, but 'despite' is followed by a noun phrase, not a clause.
questions.explanation: Correct. Although + clause; Despite + noun/gerund.

questions.question: 'Should' is used to express strong legal prohibition.
questions.explanation: Incorrect. 'Should' expresses advice. Legal prohibition requires 'mustn't'.

questions.question: When converting direct speech to indirect speech, Present Simple usually changes to Past Simple.
questions.explanation: Correct. Tense backshifting rule.

questions.question: Intransitive verbs (verbs without an object, like 'sleep' or 'arrive') can easily be made passive.
questions.explanation: Incorrect. Intransitive verbs cannot form passive voice because they have no direct object.

questions.scenario: Convert the following Present Simple narrative into Past Simple Tense: 'Every day, Paul wakes up early, eats breakfast, and catches the school bus. He studies hard and plays football with friends.'
questions.question: Question: Rewrite the entire narrative in Past Simple Tense.
questions.correctAnswer: Past Simple Narrative: 'Yesterday, Paul woke up early, ate breakfast, and caught the school bus. He studied hard and played football with friends.'
questions.explanation: Explanation: Irregular verbs (wake->woke, eat->ate, catch->caught) and regular verbs (study->studied, play->played) backshift to Past Simple V.2.

questions.scenario: A student wrote this paragraph containing 3 subject-verb agreement errors: 'The group of students are studying in the library. Neither John nor his sister have their book. Everyone in the class need to submit their assignment.' Identify and correct the 3 errors.
questions.question: Question: Identify the 3 agreement errors and provide corrections.
questions.correctAnswer: Error 1: 'group... are' -> 'group... IS' (collective noun group is singular).\nError 2: 'Neither... sister have' -> 'Neither... sister HAS' (agrees with singular sister).\nError 3: 'Everyone... need' -> 'Everyone... NEEDS' (indefinite pronoun is singular).
questions.explanation: Explanation: Collective nouns, neither...nor (closer subject), and 'Everyone' take singular verbs.

questions.topic: Active to Passive Voice Transformation Scenario
questions.scenario: Transform these 2 active sentences into passive voice: 1) 'The architect designed the modern library.' 2) 'Volunteers clean the local beach every weekend.'
questions.question: Question: Provide the correct passive voice conversions.
questions.correctAnswer: 1) Passive: 'The modern library was designed by the architect.'\n2) Passive: 'The local beach is cleaned by volunteers every weekend.'
questions.explanation: Explanation: 1) Past Simple passive = was + V.3; 2) Present Simple passive = is + V.3.

questions.topic: Direct to Indirect Speech Conversion Scenario
questions.scenario: Convert the direct dialogue into reported speech: Teacher said to Mark: 'Why are you late today, and did you finish your homework?'
questions.question: Question: Rewrite the teacher's questions as reported speech.
questions.correctAnswer: Reported Speech: 'The teacher asked Mark why he was late that day and if he had finished his homework.'
questions.explanation: Explanation: 1) Wh-question keeps wh-word with statement order and past tense (why he was late); 2) Yes/No question takes 'if/whether' with Past Perfect (if he had finished).

questions.scenario: Construct the correct question tags for these 3 statements: 1) 'She can speak three languages, _____?' 2) 'They didn't see the movie, _____?' 3) 'You're coming to the party, _____?'
questions.question: Question: Provide the 3 matching question tags.
questions.correctAnswer: 1) 'can't she?' (Positive statement -> negative tag)\n2) 'did they?' (Negative statement -> positive tag)\n3) 'aren't you?' (Positive statement -> negative tag)
questions.explanation: Explanation: Match auxiliary verb, reverse polarity (positive/negative), use pronoun.

questions.scenario: Combine each pair of sentences into one complex sentence using relative pronouns (who, which, whose): 1) 'The woman called the police. Her car was stolen.' 2) 'I read the book. It was recommended by my teacher.'
questions.question: Question: Combine the sentence pairs using relative clauses.
questions.correctAnswer: 1) 'The woman whose car was stolen called the police.' (whose = possessive)\n2) 'I read the book which/that was recommended by my teacher.' (which/that = object/thing)
questions.explanation: Explanation: Use 'whose' for possessive relationship and 'which/that' for things.

questions.scenario: Create 2 First Conditional sentences based on these situations: 1) Rain tomorrow -> Stay home. 2) Finish homework early -> Play video games.
questions.question: Question: Write 2 First Conditional (If + Present Simple, Will + V.1) sentences.
questions.correctAnswer: 1) 'If it rains tomorrow, we will stay home.'\n2) 'If I finish my homework early, I will play video games.'
questions.explanation: Explanation: First Conditional pattern: If-clause (Present Simple) + Main clause (will + V.1).

questions.scenario: Fill in the correct prepositions of time and place: 'My brother was born ___ (1) 8:30 a.m. ___ (2) July 12th ___ (3) 2012 ___ (4) a hospital ___ (5) Bangkok.'
questions.question: Question: Provide the 5 correct prepositions in order.
questions.correctAnswer:
(1) at (specific time 8:30 a.m.)
(2) on (specific date July 12th)
(3) in (year 2012)
(4) in / at (hospital)
(5) in (city Bangkok)
questions.explanation: Explanation: at time, on date, in year, in city.

questions.scenario: Proofread the passage and fix 4 grammar errors: 'Yesterday, Mary go (1) to the market and buy (2) some apples. She didn't had (3) enough money, so she borrow (4) $5 from her friend.'
questions.question: Question: List the 4 incorrect words and their corrections.
questions.correctAnswer:
1) 'go' -> 'went' (Past Simple V.2)
2) 'buy' -> 'bought' (Past Simple V.2)
3) 'had' -> 'have' (After didn't, use bare infinitive have)
4) 'borrow' -> 'borrowed' (Past Simple V.2)
questions.explanation: Explanation: Past narrative consistency and auxiliary didn't + bare infinitive.

questions.scenario: Write 3 sentences for a school safety rules poster using: 1) 'must' (rule), 2) 'mustn't' (prohibition), 3) 'should' (advice).
questions.question: Question: Formulate 3 distinct modal sentences.
questions.correctAnswer: 1) Must: 'Students must wear school uniforms every day.'\n2) Mustn't: 'Students mustn't run in the hallways.'\n3) Should: 'Students should eat healthy food during lunchtime.'
questions.explanation: Explanation: Must = obligation; Mustn't = prohibition; Should = advice.

questions.scenario: Fill in the correct articles (a, an, the, or - for zero article): '___ (1) Sun is ___ (2) star. It gives us ___ (3) light and ___ (4) heat. ___ (5) Earth revolves around it.'
questions.question: Question: Provide the 5 correct articles.
questions.correctAnswer:
(1) The (unique celestial body)
(2) a (singular countable noun starting with consonant sound)
(3) - (uncountable noun in general sense)
(4) - (uncountable noun in general sense)
(5) The (unique planet)
questions.explanation: Explanation: The Sun, a star, light (no article), heat (no article), The Earth.

questions.scenario: Choose the correct verb form (gerund -ing or infinitive to + V.1) for each sentence: 1) 'I stopped (to smoke / smoking) two years ago.' (ceased habit) 2) 'He stopped (to buy / buying) a newspaper on his way home.' (paused action to do another)
questions.question: Question: Select and explain the correct verb forms for both sentences.
questions.correctAnswer: 1) 'smoking' (stop + gerund = quit/cease habit permanently)\n2) 'to buy' (stop + infinitive = pause current activity in order to perform another action)
questions.explanation: Explanation: Stop + gerund = terminate action; Stop + infinitive = pause to do something else.

questions.scenario: Arrange the adjectives in correct order (OSASCOMP: Opinion, Size, Age, Shape, Color, Origin, Material, Purpose): 'a / wooden / beautiful / old / round / table'.
questions.question: Question: Write the adjectives in correct standard English order.
questions.correctAnswer: Correct Order: 'a beautiful old round wooden table'\n(Opinion: beautiful -> Age: old -> Shape: round -> Material: wooden).
questions.explanation: Explanation: Adjective order: Opinion -> Size -> Age -> Shape -> Color -> Origin -> Material.

questions.scenario: Edit and rewrite this sentence with correct punctuation and capitalization: 'on monday mr brown said we will travel to paris france'
questions.question: Question: Rewrite the sentence with proper capitalization, comma, and quotation marks.
questions.correctAnswer: Correct Sentence: 'On Monday, Mr. Brown said, "We will travel to Paris, France."'
questions.explanation: Explanation: Capitalize On, Monday, Mr., Brown, We, Paris, France. Add comma after Monday and said, period after Mr, quotation marks around direct quote.

questions.scenario: Complete the story with their/there/they're and its/it's: '___ (1) standing over ___ (2) with ___ (3) dog. ___ (4) a cute puppy, and ___ (5) tail is wagging fast.'
questions.question: Question: Supply the 5 correct homophones/contractions in order.
questions.correctAnswer:
(1) They're (They are)
(2) there (location)
(3) their (possessive)
(4) It's (It is)
(5) its (possessive)
questions.explanation: Explanation: They're = They are; there = place; their = possessive; It's = It is; its = possessive.

questions.question: State the formulas and provide 1 example sentence for: 1) Present Simple, 2) Present Continuous, 3) Past Simple, 4) Future Simple (will).
questions.correctAnswer:
1) Present Simple: Subject + V.1(s/es) -> She drinks tea.
2) Present Continuous: Subject + is/am/are + V.-ing -> She is drinking tea.
3) Past Simple: Subject + V.2 -> She drank tea.
4) Future Simple: Subject + will + V.1 -> She will drink tea.
questions.explanation: Evaluation based on grammatical correctness, clarity, and completeness of explanation.

questions.question: State 3 key Subject-Verb Agreement rules involving: 1) Singular vs Plural subjects, 2) 'Neither... nor', 3) Indefinite pronouns (everyone/nobody).
questions.correctAnswer: 1) Singular subjects take singular verbs; plural subjects take plural verbs (The dog runs / The dogs run).\n2) With 'Neither A nor B', the verb agrees with subject B closest to it (Neither John nor his friends ARE coming).\n3) Indefinite pronouns (everyone, nobody, somebody) always take singular verbs (Everyone IS ready).
questions.explanation: Evaluation based on grammatical correctness, clarity, and completeness of explanation.

questions.question: Explain the 3 main steps to convert an active sentence into a passive sentence. Convert: 'The mechanic fixed the red car.'
questions.correctAnswer:
Steps:
1) Move the active object to become the passive subject ('The red car').
2) Add verb 'to be' matching the active tense + V.3 of active verb ('was fixed').
3) Place active subject after 'by' ('by the mechanic').
Result: 'The red car was fixed by the mechanic.'
questions.explanation: Evaluation based on grammatical correctness, clarity, and completeness of explanation.

questions.question: Explain the tense backshift rules for converting Direct Speech to Reported Speech for: 1) Present Simple, 2) Present Continuous, 3) Past Simple. Convert: He said, 'I play tennis.'
questions.correctAnswer:
Backshift Rules:
1) Present Simple -> Past Simple
2) Present Continuous -> Past Continuous
3) Past Simple -> Past Perfect
Conversion: Direct: He said, 'I play tennis.' -> Reported: He said that he played tennis.
questions.explanation: Evaluation based on grammatical correctness, clarity, and completeness of explanation.

questions.question: Explain the 3 main rules for creating Question Tags. Provide 2 examples: 1 positive main clause, 1 negative main clause.
questions.correctAnswer:
Rules:
1) Balance polarity: Positive clause -> Negative tag; Negative clause -> Positive tag.
2) Use the same auxiliary/modal verb from the main clause.
3) Use a pronoun corresponding to the subject.
Examples:
1) Positive clause: 'She is a doctor, isn't she?'
2) Negative clause: 'They don't like coffee, do they?'
questions.explanation: Evaluation based on grammatical correctness, clarity, and completeness of explanation.

questions.topic: Prepositions of Time & Place Summary (in, on, at)
questions.question: Summarize the usage of 'in', 'on', and 'at' for both Time and Place with 1 example for each.
questions.correctAnswer:
Time:
- 'at': Specific clock time (at 5:00 p.m.)
- 'on': Specific day/date (on Monday, on July 4th)
- 'in': Month, year, season (in July, in 2026, in summer)
Place:
- 'at': Specific point/address (at school, at 10 Main St)
- 'on': Surface/street name (on the table, on Sukhumvit Road)
- 'in': Enclosed space/city/country (in the room, in Bangkok, in Thailand)
questions.explanation: Evaluation based on grammatical correctness, clarity, and completeness of explanation.

questions.question: Compare Zero Conditional and First Conditional regarding: 1) Function/Meaning, 2) Sentence Structure, 3) Provide 1 example sentence for each.
questions.correctAnswer: 1) Zero Conditional: Scientific facts/universal truths -> Structure: If + Present Simple, Present Simple. Example: If you freeze water, it turns to ice.\n2) First Conditional: Real/possible future events -> Structure: If + Present Simple, Will + V.1. Example: If it rains tomorrow, I will take an umbrella.
questions.explanation: Evaluation based on grammatical correctness, clarity, and completeness of explanation.

questions.question: Explain 4 rules for making nouns plural: 1) Regular -s, 2) -es for s/ch/sh/x, 3) -y to -ies, 4) Irregular plurals. Give 1 example for each.
questions.correctAnswer:
1) Regular: Add -s (book -> books)
2) End in s, ch, sh, x: Add -es (watch -> watches)
3) End in consonant + y: Change y to i + es (city -> cities)
4) Irregular: Change internal vowels/form (child -> children, foot -> feet)
questions.explanation: Evaluation based on grammatical correctness, clarity, and completeness of explanation.

questions.question: Differentiate Countable and Uncountable nouns. Specify which quantifiers (many, much, a few, a little) are used with each.
questions.correctAnswer: 1) Countable Nouns: Things that can be counted individually (e.g., apples, cars). Uses quantifiers 'many' and 'a few'.\n2) Uncountable Nouns: Substances/concepts that cannot be counted individually (e.g., water, milk, information). Uses quantifiers 'much' and 'a little'.
questions.explanation: Evaluation based on grammatical correctness, clarity, and completeness of explanation.

questions.question: Explain how to identify and correct 3 common grammar errors: 1) Double negative, 2) Misplaced apostrophe in possessive vs contraction, 3) Subject-verb disagreement.
questions.correctAnswer: 1) Double Negative: Avoid using two negatives together (Change 'I don't know nothing' -> 'I don't know anything').\n2) Apostrophe: Distinguish contraction (It's = It is) from possessive adjective (its = belonging to it).\n3) Subject-Verb Agreement: Match verb number to subject (Change 'The list of items are long' -> 'The list of items IS long').
questions.explanation: Evaluation based on grammatical correctness, clarity, and completeness of explanation.
